szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial Intelligence Mediates Students' Research Methodology Learning While Introducing Ethical Tensions

A qualitative study exploring how students integrate artificial intelligence into research training indicates that AI tools act as cognitive mediators, supporting proposal writing while creating pedagogical and ethical tensions. Researchers examined the lived experiences of students learning research methodology and formulating study proposals with the assistance of both general-purpose and specialized computational tools.

The study, published in BMC Medical Education, investigated how generative artificial intelligence shapes foundational research training in higher education. While artificial intelligence platforms have expanded rapidly across educational settings, empirical evidence detailing how students perceive and navigate these technologies during proposal development has remained limited.

To evaluate these dynamics, researchers adopted an experiential qualitative study design involving fourteen Medical Library and Information Science students. Each participant had documented experience employing both general-purpose and domain-specific artificial intelligence tools for learning research methodology and writing academic proposals.

Participants completed an Experience Registration Form documenting their interactions with artificial intelligence systems across core proposal milestones. The investigative team analyzed this qualitative data using thematic analysis, tracking experiences during topic selection, problem formulation, literature review preparation, and final proposal drafting.

The thematic analysis identified five overarching themes characterizing student interactions with artificial intelligence across the methodology curriculum. Participants experienced artificial intelligence as a supportive but potentially dependency-forming research companion.

Students also engaged in active negotiation when evaluating the educational value of selecting specific artificial intelligence tools. While artificial intelligence supported learning across the research process, students negotiated the benefits and risks of AI use.

The findings further revealed perceived conditions that determined student satisfaction with artificial intelligence-assisted learning environments. Students experienced artificial intelligence as a cognitive mediator that facilitated learning research methodology.

The study authors concluded that integrating critical artificial intelligence literacy into formal research methodology education is essential for academic institutions. The researchers emphasized that establishing clear institutional guidelines remains critical to ensure the responsible use of artificial intelligence in proposal writing and research training.

Students experienced artificial intelligence as a cognitive mediator that facilitated learning research methodology and introduced epistemological and ethical tensions. Across key stages of proposal development, including topic selection, problem formulation, literature review, and final proposal writing, findings demonstrated that artificial intelligence reshaped students' approaches to learning research methodology. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that artificial intelligence created new pedagogical and ethical challenges.

Additionally, findings identified perceived conditions underlying student satisfaction with artificial intelligence-assisted learning. Students negotiated the benefits and risks of artificial intelligence use. These findings underscore the importance of integrating critical artificial intelligence literacy into research methodology education and developing clear institutional guidelines for proposal writing and research training.

Subject of Research: Qualitative analysis of students using artificial intelligence for research methodology and proposal writing

Article Title: Students experiences of using artificial intelligence to learn research methodology: an experiential qualitative study

Article References: Nouri, M., Panahi, S., & Ghalavand, H. (2026). Students experiences of using artificial intelligence to learn research methodology: an experiential qualitative study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10914-3

Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Research Methodology, Higher Education, Medical Education, Qualitative Research, Proposal Writing, Thematic Analysis, Educational Technology, Academic Integrity, Cognitive Mediator, Literature Review, Medical Library and Information Science, AI Literacy, Research Training, Student Experience
